MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Service

PATIENT DETAILS
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood (EDTA)
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Diagnostic testing for suspected Merosin Deficient Congenital Muscular Dystrophy type 1A (MDC1A)

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Patient referred for molecular genetic testing due to clinical features suggestive of congenital muscular dystrophy. Elevated creatine kinase levels and muscle biopsy findings indicate possible merosin (laminin α2) deficiency.

METHODOLOGY
LAMA2 gene mutation screen performed using:
- Heteroduplex analysis for initial mutation detection
- Direct DNA sequencing of all coding exons and intron-exon boundaries
- Reference sequence: NM_000426.3
- Analysis covers >99% of reported pathogenic variants in LAMA2

RESULTS
LAMA2 Gene Analysis:
Variant detected: c.403C>T (p.Gln135X) in exon 4
Zygosity: Homozygous
Protein effect: p.Gln135X (Glutamine to stop codon at position 135)

This nonsense mutation is predicted to result in a severely truncated laminin α2 protein, lacking the majority of functional domains required for basement membrane assembly and muscle fiber stability.

INTERPRETATION
The homozygous c.403C>T (p.Gln135X) variant in LAMA2 is classified as PATHOGENIC based on:
- Nonsense mutation creating premature termination codon
- Loss of >95% of protein function
- Previously reported in patients with MDC1A
- Absent from population databases
- Consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance pattern

This result confirms the clinical diagnosis of Merosin Deficient Congenital Muscular Dystrophy type 1A (MDC1A).

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS
The p.Gln135X mutation is likely pathogenic, confirming MDC1A diagnosis. This severe early-onset muscular dystrophy is characterized by:
- Hypotonia and muscle weakness from birth
- Elevated serum creatine kinase
- White matter abnormalities on brain MRI
- Normal intellectual development in most cases
- Progressive respiratory insufficiency

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Genetic counseling to discuss inheritance pattern and recurrence risks
2. Prenatal diagnosis available for parents in future pregnancies
3. Carrier testing available for family members if appropriate
4. Multidisciplinary management including neurology, physiotherapy, and respiratory support
5. Regular monitoring of respiratory function and nutritional status
6. Consider brain MRI if not already performed

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
